Lancet Calls for Global Climate Health Emergency (Health) Israel’s general election has left both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc without a parliamentary majority, according to exit polls. Two broadcasters projected both blocs winning 51 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while another gave Netanyahu a narrow lead. Both leaders claimed victory as counting continued. ... The two Arab parties are projected to secure a record 18 or 19 seats, potentially determining who can form a government. However, only one opposition party has openly supported working with them and a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot also appears unlikely. Turnout reached 77.7%, its highest level at that stage since 1999. Around 600,000 absentee ballots, mostly from military personnel, will not be fully counted until Thursday. Once results are confirmed, Israel’s president will consult political factions before selecting a leader to attempt forming a coalition, a process that could take weeks. Another election remains possible. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere held a rare 90-minute telephone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, urging an end to the war in Ukraine. They subsequently spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. The initiative preceded planned talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi next month. The outreach exposed divisions among European leaders. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticised the lack of coordination and said she saw no signs Russia wanted peace. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson warned against dividing Europe’s position, while Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha welcomed the contact as coordinated with Kyiv. The Kremlin offered no indication of compromise, insisting Russia’s interests must be fully considered. ... The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund, a government investment vehicle previously described by US officials as a slush fund for President Vladimir Putin. An American official said the fund’s application was being assessed through established procedures as Washington seeks improved relations with Moscow and an end to the Ukraine war. ... Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino has ordered a police investigation into possible illegal foreign assistance to Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, following his defeat by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Sunday. Investigators will examine alleged contacts involving the Rockbridge Network, a US donor group co-founded by Vice President JD Vance, and Brazilian intermediaries. Brazilian law prohibits foreign campaign funding and other economic assistance. The allegations arose from complaints by Bolsonaro’s opponents, including former presidential candidate Renan Santos. Rockbridge denied involvement, saying Brazilians claiming to represent the network had falsely presented themselves as its agents. Dino emphasised that the investigation did not establish wrongdoing. ... The Pentagon has put the cost of the US war against Iran at $47.1 billion through 16 October, with munitions accounting for more than 60% of spending. The figure exceeds Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s July estimate of $37.5 billion by more than 25%, even as President Donald Trump holds back from restarting major combat operations. The military has used $29 billion in munitions, drawing down critical weapons stockpiles and supplies from US commands in Asia and Europe. Another $6.1 billion has gone towards replacing damaged or destroyed aircraft and equipment. More than 50,000 troops are assigned to the mission. ... The European Commission is proposing rules requiring member states to prepare for a 3C rise in global temperatures by 2100 and identify which authorities are responsible for managing climate risks. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said cutting emissions alone would not protect citizens from increasingly severe heatwaves, floods and wildfires. Europe is warming at roughly twice the global average. The proposals would bring climate scenarios into decisions on infrastructure and public investment. Hoekstra estimated that extreme weather caused more than €100 billion in economic damage across Europe this summer, while high temperatures contributed to approximately 50,000 deaths. Financing remains a central gap. The Commission estimates that adaptation will require €70 billion annually until 2050, but the proposed framework includes no new funding. ... Researchers behind the Lancet Countdown report have called on the World Health Organization and United Nations to declare climate change a global health emergency, warning that health risks are accelerating faster than efforts to address them. The report estimates that heat caused three million deaths worldwide between 2016 and 2023, with 68% attributable to climate change. Heat-related deaths reached a record 710,000 in 2023, more than 70% linked to human-caused warming. The researchers also identified growing risks from drought, extreme rainfall and conditions favouring dengue transmission. They argue that an emergency declaration could strengthen health surveillance, early warnings and coordinated action.

items.title: Fed meeting live updates: Federal Reserve weighs elevated inflation, midterm elections as October meeting kicks off
items.excerpt: Yahoo Finance Updated Wed, October 28, 2026 at 9:27 AM EDT 1 min read ... The Federal Reserve kicked off its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday as elevated inflation continues to pose a problem for central bankers who nevertheless seem reluctant to hike rates this month. Fed watchers expect the central bank to keep benchmark rates in the 3.75% to 4% range, with bond traders pricing in a less than 10% chance of a hike on Wednesday, per CME Group. A rate hike in December appears far more likely, however, according to the Fed's dot plot and fed funds futures. Although recent inflation data came in hotter than expected, several officials' remarks suggest the Fed will hold rates this month to continue assessing additional data. The proximity of the October meeting to the US midterm elections next Tuesday is also seen as a deterrent to bold monetary policy moves. With the Fed holding rates steady seen as all but given, the focus is on what Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will say at his post-FOMC-meeting press conference. Warsh has deliberately avoided telegraphing future Fed policy moves, but hot inflation could elicit more insight from him into the path forward.

items.title: Treasury yields tick higher ahead of Fed interest rate decision
items.excerpt: Published Wed, Oct 28 2026 5:22 AM EDT Hugh Leask Bond yields moved higher early Wednesday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's latest monetary policy decision, due later in the session. The 10-year Treasury note Add To Watchlist yield — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was more than 2 basis points higher at 5.0134%. The yield on the 2-year Treasury Add To Watchlist note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, was up 1 basis point at 4.7494%. Meanwhile, the yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys Add To Watchlist — which tend to move on geopolitical events — was also up by more than 1 basis point at 5.3200%. One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another. The moves come as traders price in a 90.6% chance that the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee will leave interest rates unchanged at 375-400 basis points, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. Investors will be closely watching Fed chairman Kevin Warsh's statement following the decision for signals on future monetary policy projections. Expectations for a 25 basis points hike at the Fed's next meeting on Dec. 9 currently stand at 76.5%. More economic data is due Thursday. Personal consumption expenditures index — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — as well as the quarterly GDP growth rate and personal income and spending data will offer investors additional insights into the domestic economy and inflation picture.

items.title: Soaring Energy Prices Push Inflation Higher
items.excerpt: The bulk of the increase stemmed directly from energy prices, which have shot higher this year because of the war with Iran. Gasoline prices, which in late September rose to the highest level in four months at nearly $4.50 a gallon, surged 9.1 percent for the month. That accounted for more than half of the overall monthly increase in prices. They are up 34.2 percent over the past year. Fuel oil prices, used for heating in many homes in the northeast, have also shot higher, rising 15.3 percent in September, or 74.2 percent on an annual basis. “Core” inflation, which excludes volatile energy and food prices, edged higher as well, but by a smaller magnitude.

items.title: Live Updates: 2026 midterm campaigns make final push before Election Day as early voters hit the polls
items.excerpt: Updated on: October 28, 2026 / 9:29 AM EDT / CBS News ## What to know leading up to Election Day 2026 - Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, and early voting is currently underway throughout the country. More than 35 million people have voted early as of Tuesday, according to the University of Florida Election Lab. - All 435 House seats plus 35 Senate seats will be on the ballot, and voters in 36 states will be electing governors. - CBS News' Battleground Tracker estimates that Democrats have an edge in the race for control of the House. Senate control could be decided by voters in a handful of toss-up states ranging from Alaska to Maine. - President Trump heads to Ohio today to campaign for GOP Sen. Jon Husted and Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican candidate for governor, part of a weekslong blitz that brought him to Texas on Tuesday and Mississippi on Monday. ... ## Inside Majority Leader John Thune's push to save his Senate majority Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a South Dakota Republican, has for two years led his colleagues through unforgiving terrain, trying to do two things at once: advance the president's agenda and preserve the Senate's independence. Now, next week's midterm election stands as the clearest test yet of whether that balancing act has paid off. A map that once favored Senate Republicans has turned perilous amid an unpopular war with Iran and stubbornly high gas prices, and their low-key leader faces questions voters are about to answer: Has Thune's approach worked — for Republicans, and for him? And has it been enough to keep the majority? ... ## Murkowski backs Democratic candidate for governor Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski, who has bucked President Trump and the GOP, on Tuesday backed the Democratic candidate for governor in Alaska, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, who is widely referred to as JKT. "JKT is a young Alaskan with a view and a perspective that I think Alaska needs right now," Murkowski told Anchorage's KTUU-TV on Tuesday. She said Kriess-Tomkins will "work with the legislature," adding that will be important for the state's at-large representative and senators in Washington, D.C. In a news release, Murkowski encouraged "Alaskans of every political stripe, whether Republicans, independents, or Democrats" to consider Kriess-Tomkins, adding "Alaska needs leaders who will put our state first, and I'm proud to support them." ... ## Trump campaigns for Ken Paxton in Texas President Trump held two rallies in Texas on Tuesday to campaign for Attorney General Ken Paxton, who is running for Senate, and several House candidates, including Rep. Monica De La Cruz in South Texas. The campaign stops in Corpus Christi and Lubbock came as Republicans fight to stave off their first statewide loss in Texas in more than 30 years. CBS News considers the race between Paxton and Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico a toss-up, even though Mr. Trump won Texas by more than 13 points two years ago. Talarico held a rally nearby in Lubbock. During his visit to Lubbock, the president touted his record and offered his familiar refrain for voters to "pretend I'm on the ballot." ... ## 47 battleground House seats could determine which party wins control Control of the House of Representatives will come down to a number of battleground seats. CBS News has identified 47 House districts that will likely determine which party will have the majority. Of those seats, 20 are currently held by Democrats and 27 are held by Republicans. Republicans currently hold a razor-thin majority, with 218 seats, plus an independent who normally caucuses with them. Democrats hold 214 seats. There are two vacancies. CBS News' Battleground Tracker model estimated on Sunday that Democrats are on track to take control of the House with 229 seats. There is still a path for the GOP to keep the House: The Battleground Tracker's estimates ranged from 215 Democratic seats — which would give Republicans a narrow majority — to 237 seats. ... ## The 10 Senate races that will decide control of the Senate Republicans currently hold 53 seats in the Senate, while Democrats have 47. CBS News has identified 10 key seats this election that could determine control of the Senate. Seven of those seats are held by Republicans: Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, Kansas, Iowa, Texas and Alaska. The other three are held by Democrats: New Hampshire, Michigan and Georgia.

items.title: Trump fights for votes in Texas and deadlock in Israeli election: Morning Rundown
items.excerpt: ## James Talarico faces off against Trump in dueling Texas rallies In reliably red Lubbock, Texas, people waited for hours in lines that stretched for blocks to see Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Less than three miles away, a similar scene unfolded for President Donald Trump, as he sought to boost the Republican Senate candidate, state Attorney General Ken Paxton. Yesterday’s dueling rallies in the city, which has a population of less than 300,000, underscored the high stakes in a Senate race that could see the Republican Party lose its grip on Texas. At Talarico’s rally, Democrats panned the economy, high gas prices and closures of rural hospitals. The Senate candidate called Paxton corrupt and sought to tie him to Elon Musk, who has significant business interests in the state. For Trump and Paxton, the stop in Lubbock was their second of the day, having held an earlier rally in Corpus Christi. At the evening event, Trump cast Talarico as a Second Amendment-hating, meat-loathing extremist out of touch with everyday Texans. Paxton leaned on Trump’s support, calling him “the greatest president of my lifetime.” And in a potential sign that Republicans were looking to attract more voters, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has generally held higher approval ratings than others in the administration, was given a speaking part. ... ## Israel’s election has no clear winner — but Netanyahu looks far from ... When Israelis awoke on Wednesday, it seemed that their future had taken another twist overnight: Results that had looked like a narrow loss for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu when they went to bed now pointed to a narrow lead by dawn. There is still no obvious winner, with uncertainty set to follow the country’s first election since the Hamas-led attack of Oct. 7, 2023. The votes are still being counted, and Israel’s Central Elections Commission said final results likely won’t be known until tomorrow. But the preliminary tallies from this pivotal contest still point to one clear outcome: Netanyahu suffered significant losses but he didn’t really lose. Still, the Israeli public dealt Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister for nearly 20 of the past 30 years, a notable electoral setback. With more than 84% of the votes counted, Netanyahu’s coalition, the most right-wing in Israeli history, would be diminished from 64 members to only 54, short of the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government. He appears to have eked out a slight advantage over the bloc led by his main rival, former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, in contrast to the initial projection from exit polls on Tuesday night. items.excerpt: - AP - Oct 28, 2026 - Oct 28, 2026 Updated 44 mins ago California appeals court upholds actor Danny Masterson's rape convictions LOS ANGELES (AP) — A California appeals court has upheld actor Danny Masterson’s convictions and long prison sentence for raping two women at his home in 2003. The three-judge panel on Tuesday unanimously found that the “That ’70s Show” actor had failed to demonstrate that the lower court made errors that would warrant granting him a new trial. Masterson was convicted in 2023 of raping two women at his home two decades earlier. He was sentenced to 30 years to life in prison. His attorneys said in an emailed statement Tuesday that they would seek review at the California Supreme Court. Susan Saint James, Emmy-winning actor of 'McMillan & Wife' and 'Kate & Allie,' dies at 80 LOS ANGELES (AP) — Susan Saint James, known for her roles in “McMillan & Wife” and “Kate & Allie,” has died at 80. People magazine reports she passed away Monday after a battle with pancreatic cancer. Born in Los Angeles, she started modeling in Paris as a teenager and later signed with Universal Studios. She gained fame in the 1970s and 1980s, earning multiple Emmy nominations. Saint James retired to focus on family but occasionally appeared on TV. She was a longtime supporter of the Special Olympics and leaves behind her husband, children, and extended family. Taylor Swift, Lyle Lovett and more inducted into Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Taylor Swift has been inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, alongside Lyle Lovett, Shawn Camp, Lee Thomas Miller, Bruce Channel and J.I. Allison. Swift signed her first publishing deal in Nashville at the age of 14. She returned to the city on Monday during the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame annual gala celebration. She said it was an incredible honor to be inducted and described soaking up the lessons from other writers like a sponge. Also honored was country music icon George Strait with the organization's Career Maker Award. He said the songwriters helped to make his career. Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show at SoFi Stadium in Southern California LOS ANGELES (AP) — Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl halftime show on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The NFL, Apple Music, and Roc Nation announced the news Monday night. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he always wanted Jay-Z to perform when the time felt right. Jay-Z expressed excitement about the opportunity, calling it a dream come true. His Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to produce entertainment presentations, including the halftime show. Jay-Z, who has won 25 Grammy Awards, will perform at the stadium where he recently celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album, “Reasonable Doubt.” Andrea Bocelli concerts in Indonesia to proceed despite opposition from Muslim clerics JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli's concerts in Indonesia will proceed despite opposition from the country's top Muslim clerical body. The Indonesian Ulema Council demanded the cancellation due to Bocelli's past support for Israel. Indonesia, a strong supporter of Palestinians, does not have formal diplomatic relations with Israel. The concerts are scheduled for October 31 at Borobudur Temple and November 3 in Jakarta. Promoter Shoemaker Live insists the events will support Indonesia's tourism and culture sectors. Bocelli plans to dedicate songs to humanity and world peace. The council argues the concerts could hurt Indonesians who support Palestinians. After pushback, the Dutch reverse course and withdraw from Eurovision again AMSTERDAM (AP) — The Netherlands is withdrawing from participating in the Eurovision Song Contest, reversing a decision in September to return to the show. NPO, the umbrella organization for public broadcasters in the country announced in September it would send a performer to the event, after a subsidiary had said a month earlier it would boycott the contest for a second year. Earlier this month, hundreds of NPO employees sent a letter opposing Dutch participation. A number of prominent Dutch media personalities also publicly objected to the move. Movie Review: In 'Everest: The Other Side,' tragedy and triumph intermingle on the peaks of Nepal AP Film Writer Jake Coyle writes in his latest review that the film “Everest: The Other Side” is as much a document of tragedy and grief as it is of extreme sport. Hike up and ski down was Jim Morrison’s relatively straightforward dream, albeit not on your typical ski hill. Morrison and his partner Hilaree Nelson aspired to summit Mount Everest on the north face, something only five people had ever done. And they wanted to ski down, which no one had ever done. “Everest: The Other Side,” by “Free Solo” filmmakers Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, is the big-screen chronicle of their mission. Japanese manga artist Tetsuya Chiba, known for his boxing masterpiece 'Ashita no Joe,' dies at 87 TOKYO (AP) — Tetsuya Chiba, a legendary Japanese manga artist best known for his boxing series “Ashita no Joe,” or “Fighting for Tomorrow,” has died. He was 87. Chiba’s masterpiece “Ashita no Joe” series, depicting an aspiring young generation during Japan’s postwar era, became a national sensation. The series was so popular that fans even attended a mock funeral for the protagonist’s rival. Chiba was also a vocal supporter of peace and freedom of expression, telling stories of his harrowing memories of war as a child in his autobiographical stories and manga. Chiba’s publisher, Kodansha Ltd., said Tuesday that the artist died at a Tokyo hospital last Thursday. Music Review: Nickelback is in familiar form on cameo-heavy 'Everything Under the Sun' Nickelback’s 11th studio album “Everything Under the Sun” is a mix of hard-rock anthems, radio-friendly hits, and emotional ballads with a few surprises. The Canadian rockers mostly stick to their successful formula, which has been both criticized and celebrated for over 30 years. The Associated Press' Dennis Waszak Jr. says in his review that the album out Friday is a showcase of everything Nickelback does best. Highlights on the 12-track album include the high-energy “Rattle The Cage” and rock ballads “I Already Know” and “Make Me Love You.” Guest appearances include Sammy Hagar and actor Ryan Reynolds. But those looking for more than their formula may not enjoy it.
